title: 把品牌规范落到七类接触点：Low Tide 自然酒吧
summary: 按给定的颜色、字体、字标和波浪线辅助图形，把自然酒吧 Low Tide 的规范应用到官网首页、A4 菜单、三张 Instagram 帖子、杯垫、托特包、名片和橱窗贴，交付一份带可开关标注层的 HTML 总览。

source.title: 如何用 AutoClaw 设计专家落地品牌视觉规范：品牌设计实战
source.notes: 提示词用原文实际提交的英文版。原文交付单个 HTML 总览；复现时一次交付超出单轮输出上限，所以按接触点拆成多个 HTML 分四轮交付，最后的总览板用各件的截图拼成并带可开关标注层。Gloock / Work Sans / DM Mono 通过 Google Fonts 加载，酒款和价格由模型虚构。

turns.label: Prompt · guidelines and homepage
turns.prompt:
Here are the brand guidelines for Low Tide, a natural wine bar in Red Hook, Brooklyn. Please apply them exactly to the touchpoints below.
Colors: Tide Navy #14213D as primary, Oyster #EDE6DA as background, Kelp #4E6E4E, and Sunset Coral #F2795B as an accent that never takes more than 10% of a composition. Type: Gloock for display, always in sentence case; Work Sans for text; DM Mono for prices and labels. Logo: the lowercase wordmark "low tide" with a wave line beneath it, clear space equal to the height of the "l". Graphic device: horizontal wavy lines of varying density, like a tide chart, never rotated. Voice: dry, witty, short, e.g. "Wine, mostly."
The touchpoints are: a homepage at 1440 (hero, this week's pours, Tuesday tastings and Sunday oysters, reservation CTA, map); an A4 menu with 12 wines by the glass (grape, region, price) and 6 snacks; three Instagram posts at 1080×1350 (a new bottle arrival, an event announcement, a quote); a 100mm round coaster; a tote bag; a business card; and storefront window vinyl.
Show everything on one overview board and then each piece individually, with a toggleable annotation layer that points out which rule drives each design decision. Don't introduce a single color or font that isn't in the guidelines.

Build it as separate HTML files over a few replies. In this reply, deliver the homepage. I will ask for the other pieces next.
turns.reply_html:
The homepage is below. Notes on how the rules shaped it follow the file.

low-tide-homepage.page.html

The page, top to bottom (exactly 2400px):

  • Navigation: the wordmark, nav links in DM Mono, a "Notes" toggle and a navy "Book a table" button.
  • Hero: "Wine, mostly." set in large Gloock on Tide Navy. Opening hours are drawn as a small tide chart, and a coral sun sets into a band of tide lines.
  • This week's pours: four wine cards. Names are in Gloock, regions and notes in Work Sans, and glass and bottle prices in DM Mono.
  • Tuesday tastings and Sunday oysters: a Kelp panel and a Navy panel side by side, each with a simple line illustration.
  • Reservation: "Book a table. Or don't." with the page's main coral button.
  • Find us: address, hours and transit next to a drawn map of Red Hook. The water uses the same tide lines and a small coral pin marks the bar.
  • Footer: one short strip.

Annotations: click "Notes" in the navigation or press N. Opening the file with #notes at the end of the address starts with them on.

  • There are 16 numbered notes, each with a leader line to the element it explains and the guideline that drives it.
  • The dashed box around the logo is the clear space. It is measured live as the height of the "l" in Gloock at the size used.
  • A summary card shows the four swatches, the three fonts and a live coral meter. Coral comes to roughly 1% of the page against the 10% cap.

Brand rules:

  • Colors: only the four hex values appear anywhere, including the hover states, map, annotation layer and text selection. There are no tints, transparency or default browser colors.
  • Gloock: every Gloock line is in sentence case. The wordmark is lowercase because the guidelines define it that way.
  • Wave lines: they are generated flat and always horizontal. The spacing tightens toward the bottom to vary the density.

Placeholders and annotation layer:

  • Details to replace: the address (312 Van Brunt St), the phone number, the Instagram handle and the wine list are placeholders.
  • Default view: the screenshot shows the clean page with notes off.
  • Overlap risk: I couldn't preview the page, so with notes on a card may land over a heading. They are placed in code, so moving one is a one-line fix.

Next: in later replies I'll keep the same structure for the menu, the three posts, the coaster, the tote bag, the business card, the window vinyl and the overview board.

turns.label: Self-check
turns.prompt: Here are the images rendered from the files you just delivered (SVGs via librsvg, HTML as a browser screenshot of the top of the page), downscaled. Check them as a designer would before a client review: clipped or overlapping text, text that renders as boxes or in a fallback font, broken layout, empty areas, anything that breaks the brief's rules. If something needs fixing, deliver the corrected files under the same names. If everything is ready, say so in one or two sentences and deliver nothing.
turns.reply_html:
I found four defects in the screenshot and fixed them all in the file below:

  • Tasting notes on the wine cards: each note rendered as a bordered box on top of the wine name. The cards' .note class was also used by the annotation cards, so they picked up those styles. I renamed it .taste and limited the annotation styles to the notes layer.
  • "Opening hours, charted" label: the hero's label positioning also applied to the label inside the hours card. That pushed it under "Today's tide". It's now limited to the hero's own label.
  • Hero subtitle: it ran to three lines, left "Brunt." on its own line and sat against the buttons. I cut it to two lines, since the days are already on the hours card. I also added more space below the headline.
  • Map label: "Van Brunt St" ran into the location pin. It now sits further down the street, below the pin.

low-tide-homepage.page.html

turns.label: A4 menu and Instagram posts
turns.prompt: Now deliver the A4 menu and the three Instagram posts.
turns.reply_html:
The A4 menu and the three Instagram posts are below, in four files.

How to see the annotations. The posts and the menu can't carry a visible button without spoiling the artwork. Each file's "Notes" toggle stays hidden in the top-right corner and appears when you hover over that corner. Pressing N or adding #notes to the address also works. Each annotation has a numbered leader line to the element it explains and names the rule behind it. A small summary card lists the palette and the three fonts, and shows a live coral meter against the 10% cap.

What each piece does:

  • Menu (A4). A navy header with "By the glass" in Gloock and the setting coral sun from the homepage.
    • The 12 wines sit in two columns: "Bright and white" and "Skins and reds."
    • Each row gives the grape in Gloock, the region in Work Sans, a one-line tasting note in Kelp and the price in DM Mono.
    • The 6 snacks sit in a grid underneath. A navy footer carries the hours and the weekly events.
  • New bottle post. "Something washed up." A Kelp-green bottle floats in the tide-line sea, like a message in a bottle. A small coral "Just in" sticker sits on the label. Prices and wine details are in DM Mono.
  • Event post. "Five from the Jura." It shows five drawn wine glasses, each filled lower than the last, so the tide goes out across the tasting. A coral "$25 / 5 pours" stamp sits beside the headline, and the date and time are set as DM Mono labels.
  • Quote post. An overheard exchange: "I only drink natural wine." / "So, wine?" The reply is set larger as the punchline, with the coral sun setting into the tide below.

Coral use: coral stays between about 0.3% and 2% of each piece. Only the four brand hex values and the three brand fonts appear anywhere.

low-tide-menu.a4.html

low-tide-post-new-bottle.post.html

low-tide-post-event.post.html

low-tide-post-quote.post.html

turns.label: Self-check
turns.prompt: Here are the images rendered from the files you just delivered (SVGs via librsvg, HTML as a browser screenshot of the top of the page), downscaled. Check them as a designer would before a client review: clipped or overlapping text, text that renders as boxes or in a fallback font, broken layout, empty areas, anything that breaks the brief's rules. If something needs fixing, deliver the corrected files under the same names. If everything is ready, say so in one or two sentences and deliver nothing.
turns.reply_html:
Three of the four pieces are ready. The event post had one bug: the details row showed three stacked hairlines instead of one rule per column. The selector .details div also matched the label and value inside each column, so each of them drew its own top border. Changing it to .details > div fixes it. The corrected file is below; the menu, new bottle post and quote post are unchanged.

low-tide-post-event.post.html

turns.label: Coaster, tote, card, window vinyl
turns.prompt: Now deliver the 100mm round coaster, the tote bag, the business card and the storefront window vinyl, presented together on one sheet.
turns.reply_html:
The sheet is below. It shows the coaster, tote bag, business card and window vinyl together on one 1440×1800 page.

low-tide-print-signage.sheet.html

The sheet, piece by piece:

  • Coaster: shown at 100 mm, front and back, with a dimension line under the front.
    • The front is Navy with the wordmark and a coral sun setting into tide lines.
    • The back is Oyster and reads "Same again? Nod at the bar. We'll notice." Its Kelp tide lines are clipped by the circle rather than bent to follow it.
    • Specs underline the voice: "2,000. Some will walk."
  • Tote bag: Oyster canvas on a Kelp field, printed in two spot colors, Navy and Coral. It reads "Holds three bottles. (or two and a baguette)" above a tide band with the sun. The specs beside it end with "Wash: Cold. Like the Gamay."
  • Business card: 89 × 51 mm. The front is Navy with the wordmark and tide lines. The back is Oyster and uses all three typefaces in their set roles: the name in Gloock, the title in Work Sans and the contact details in DM Mono.
  • Window vinyl: shown on a drawn storefront with a Kelp facade.
    • The glass carries the Oyster cut-vinyl wordmark, "Wine, mostly." and the hours.
    • Along the bottom of the glass is a band of tide lines with the coral sun, which also works as a privacy strip.
    • The door reads "Push. Gently." and carries the hours in DM Mono.

Annotations:

  • Toggle: use the Notes button in the header, press N, or add #notes to the address.
  • Notes: there are 16 numbered notes. With them on, a dashed box is also drawn around every wordmark on every object to show its clear space. Each box is measured live as the height of the "l" at that size, so you can see the rule holds on the coaster circle and the top of the window.

Brand rules:

  • Coral: about 0.15% of the sheet in total. It appears once per object, always as the setting sun.
  • Palette and type: only the four hex values and the three fonts appear anywhere.

Placeholders to confirm: the cardholder's name and contact details. The tote canvas is specified as "matched to Oyster", which needs confirming with your supplier, since undyed canvas varies.

turns.label: Self-check
turns.prompt: Here are the images rendered from the files you just delivered (SVGs via librsvg, HTML as a browser screenshot of the top of the page), downscaled. Check them as a designer would before a client review: clipped or overlapping text, text that renders as boxes or in a fallback font, broken layout, empty areas, anything that breaks the brief's rules. If something needs fixing, deliver the corrected files under the same names. If everything is ready, say so in one or two sentences and deliver nothing.
turns.reply_html:
The sheet has two issues before client review, both fixed in the file below.

  • Coaster back label: "LOW TIDE · 312 VAN BRUNT ST" ran to the curve and touched the circle's edge. It now reads "312 VAN BRUNT ST", which fits inside the circle with room to spare. The wordmark on the front already names the bar.
  • Sentence asides set in the wrong font: "Nod at the bar. We'll notice." on the coaster and "(or two and a baguette)" on the tote are running text, not labels. The guidelines reserve DM Mono for prices and labels, so both are now in Work Sans. I updated the two annotations that described them.

low-tide-print-signage.sheet.html

turns.label: Overview board with annotation layer
turns.prompt: Now deliver the overview board: everything together first, then each piece individually, with the toggleable annotation layer that points out which rule drives each design decision.
turns.reply_html:
The overview board is below. The screenshots from your earlier rounds load as images, and every image links to its HTML file.

low-tide-overview.board.html

The board, top to bottom (1440×2400):

  • "Everything, mostly." The header carries the wordmark, a Notes toggle and the headline in Gloock.
  • 01 · All together: all six files shown in one collage at their real proportions, with no gaps. The homepage sits on the left. The menu and the print sheet sit top right, with the three posts below them. Each image is numbered and links to its file.
  • 02 · One at a time: a card for each piece with its screenshot and the three rules that did the most work on it. Each card also has a small coral meter for that piece and two links: "Open →" and "With notes →". The second opens the file with its own annotation layer already on.
  • Footer: the same tide strip as the homepage booking section, then the palette and fonts.

Annotations: click "Notes" in the header, press N or add #notes to the address.

  • There are 12 numbered notes with leader lines. They point into the collage to show each rule repeating across pieces: the coral sun, Navy as primary, Kelp for events, the wordmark's clear space, mono prices and horizontal tide lines.
  • A summary card lists the four swatches, the three fonts and each piece's coral share. The event post is the highest at about 1.9%, well under the 10% cap.

Brand rules: the board itself uses only the four hex values and the three fonts. Its only coral is the meter fills.

Default view: the screenshot shows the clean board with notes off.
